nodes.label: ADR 0019: Ambiguity is judged on marks and resolved by policy
nodes.rationale: mark-diacritics should make unmarked text student-friendly with as little manual work as possible. Leaving every ambiguous key untouched left 889 of 967 keys undecided. Ambiguity is judged on diphthong-canonical marks so hyphen, case, and eth/thorn variants collapse, standard element spellings remove editorial mark pairs, and an explicit policy guesses only where that is safe. The ambiguous list in the file is not rewritten because the index is curated data. Decisions 2 to 8 are implemented; decision 1 is still marked proposed.

nodes.label: mark-diacritics ambiguity policy
nodes.rationale: auto is the CLI default: apply the union of marks when some BT option is hyphenated or the key has 8 or more letters, except when the marks differ only before a BT hyphen on a non-standard element, where the difference may be lexical. leave keeps today's report-only behavior. union is an opt-in guess and skips letters where macron, breve, and diaeresis conflict. Guessed tokens stay in the ambiguity report with applied_form and policy so the user can veto them. Completed keys are never guessed. MacronApplicator defaults to leave; the CLI defaults to auto.

nodes.label: Standard element spellings
nodes.rationale: Some prefixes and compound elements have one standard spelling because BT's mark variants are editorial or scribal, not a difference in meaning. The hand-edited file wyrdcraeft/etc/diacritic/standard_elements.txt maps unmarked elements to plain a-, for-, fore-, ge-, and bonde, or to marked hīrēd-, bēacen-, and ōþ-. gebed- and ge-bēd- stay separate because it is not certain every unmarked form contains bēd. An element counts only where every differing BT option writes a hyphen directly after it or around a suffix, so ge-an and gēan stay apart. The source keeps marks it already wrote. The user accepted that unique entries change too, including 823 ā- forms losing that mark.

nodes.label: ambiguous_completed
nodes.rationale: A key in ambiguous_completed was decided by the user to be genuinely ambiguous or curated. Neither auto nor union applies marks to it, the importer never touches it, and a completed key does not collapse even when its options agree. MacronIndex must carry the set; without it the applicator cannot tell curated keys from undecided ones.

nodes.label: auto-policy precision on labeled ambiguity decisions
nodes.rationale: The ADR reports 79% precision for a first hyphen-or-length rule and 64% after the non-standard-prefix guard, on different key sets that it says are not directly comparable. Implementation notes later pin 74% (29 of 137 same-word keys marked, 10 of 78 homographs wrongly marked; union 52%). The 8-letter threshold was fit on a small sample skewed to the start of the alphabet, so the figure is likely optimistic. Which percentage is the operative precision is uncertain.

nodes.label: mark-diacritics order of operations
nodes.rationale: Decision 1 says: look up with normalize_old_english, reduce each reference to a diphthong-canonical mark pattern, apply standard elements, collapse options that agree, apply the ambiguity policy, then transfer marks onto the source. The heading marks this order proposed, while decisions 2 to 8 are implemented and the implementation notes describe that same pipeline in code.
